contract.behavior: Observe three adopted mechanism files without changes; compare semantics with KB and actual package contracts.
contract.authority: Host owns schemas, migration callbacks, queries, budgets, retry and product error handling; observer owns receipts only.
contract.state_ordering: Same actor serializes synchronous closure execution; write result follows save; rollback precedes thrown write error; migration version advances after callback return.
contract.envelopes: Migration version graph, callback/context mutation, bounded UI operations and cancellation are reviewed; arbitrary host closures are outside enforcement.
contract.failure: No failed/unrun/static observation becomes runtime or production success; no reset or destructive recovery.
contract.consumers: Declared memberships TchopApp and TchopAppOcean only; shipping call sites not read or established.

supported_paths.supported: Groups by fromVersion, chooses smallest toVersion, rejects non-increasing chosen edge and missing edge; persists version only after callback returns.
supported_paths.unknown: Complete-path validation, equality to target, valid app-supplied graph, database/version-store crash atomicity, actual shipped schema migration.

supported_paths.supported: No data deletion/reset path exists in these files. Callback failure does not advance its version.
supported_paths.unknown: Physical durability and reopen, storage failure, SwiftData schema migration and every historical schema; not executed here.

supported_paths.supported: Result returned after save; thrown operation/save failures roll back current context; DatabaseError stays typed; other errors are wrapped.
supported_paths.unknown: Callbacks can save themselves or produce external effects; rollback is context-wide, not an undo of previously committed work. No automatic retry/idempotency; main context may already contain caller edits.

supported_paths.supported: Read executes on owning context; actor Result:Sendable constrains returned values.
supported_paths.unknown: Read-only is closure discipline: mutable ModelContext can be mutated; read has no rollback barrier; no actual violating caller established.

supported_paths.supported: A closure-thrown CancellationError follows rollback for writes and gets wrapped as fetchFailed/transactionFailed; cancellation flag alone does not cause these methods to abort. Async forwarding stays MainActor.
supported_paths.unknown: Whether any shipping caller relies on CancellationError matching or performs cancellation checks; flag timing, latency and post-save cancellation unobserved.

supported_paths.supported: ModelActor owns worker context; MainActor owns mainContext manager/migration runner. Synchronous operation bodies have no suspension in manager code. MainActor is intentional context ownership.
supported_paths.unknown: Actor construction executor, actual workloads, merge/refresh policy and cross-context callers; actor isolation does not itself prove off-main performance.

supported_paths.evidence: Core:41-49; actor/main catch blocks; package README ownership; scoped PBX memberships
supported_paths.supported: Unsupported operation fails before invoking body; typed database errors preserved; generic errors stringified. Both host memberships observed.
supported_paths.unknown: Error descriptions can carry caller data; no logging/PII exposure established. Compilation or target membership proves no shipping invocation; no broad safety/release claim.

findings.applicability: applicable to public mechanism; shipping exposure unknown
findings.kind: KB cancellation-contract mismatch, previously disclosed in required main plan
findings.scenario: Caller closure cooperatively throws CancellationError; catch-all wraps it. A caller matching CancellationError cannot recognize cancellation through this API.
findings.impact: Public error taxonomy loses cancellation identity; no confirmed shipped user-facing failure asserted.
findings.target: Keep write rollback and preserve CancellationError identity at the boundary, or establish an explicit authorized cancellation-as-failure contract.
findings.verification_required: If separately authorized, targeted exact-source read/write CancellationError assertions plus caller mapping review; no tests created/run here.
findings.disposition: Report to integrator; observer cannot fix; no blind discovery claim.

recommendations.case: With current=0,target=1 and an edge 0->2, callback/version can reach2. Multiple outgoing edges use a greedy smallest destination, not complete-path validation.
recommendations.disposition: Validate/document host-produced forward graph, destination envelope and duplicate-branch policy before adoption expansion; not a shipped production defect without accepted graph/caller evidence.

recommendations.case: Successful database write and version marker are separate; multiple writes or external callback effects may precede callback failure.
recommendations.disposition: Host needs idempotent steps/checkpointing and explicit downgrade/failure/reopen policy. Do not claim whole-step atomicity, crash recovery or preservation from callback return.
Document read-no-mutation and clean/main-context pending-edit discipline; managed objects/context must stay on owner. Possible misuse remains hypothetical absent consumers.

Future permitted iPhone18.2+27 migration/preservation/reopen and cancellation fixtures must use current source. Physical/iPad/actual VoiceOver OMITTED_BY_USER. Existing main-plan fixture conclusions are history/priming, not independent evidence read by this arm.
